Genetic engineering is as always the technology that has supposedly huge potential, yet invariably results in extremely modest practical results. I think the primary issue is that there is a complete and utter lack of understanding in the field about causality. It is 100% correlations. Genetic engineering is like trying to program a computer by randomly soldering different spots on the motherboard and seeing what happens, or trying to understand what's going on by seeing what areas on the processor get hottest when different sorts of programs are running. And the brain is presumably some orders of magnitude more complex than basic computers today making this sort of exercise even more ultimately futile.
